blocks.text: Performing a hypothesis test follows a clear process (Fig 7.1): define the hypotheses, collect data carefully, calculate the test statistic, compare the result with the criterion and make a decision. Following the steps reduces errors and keeps the test fair.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Testing follows clear steps: data is collected and analysed, results are compared with criteria, and conclusions are drawn carefully.

items: State the null and alternative hypotheses.
Calculate the test statistic and find the p-value.
Decide: if p < alpha, reject H0; otherwise do not reject H0.

blocks.alt: Four stacked boxes joined by arrows: 1 state H0 and H1, 2 set significance level alpha, 3 collect sample data, 4 compute test statistic and p-value. Two arrows lead to the decisions: p-value < alpha, reject H0 (evidence for H1); and p-value >= alpha, fail to reject H0. A note says 'fail to reject' is safer wording than 'accept'.
blocks.caption: The steps of hypothesis testing (original diagram after Fig 7.1).
blocks.long_description: The book's figure says 'accept' when p > alpha; statisticians prefer 'fail to reject H0', because a test can only show that the evidence was not strong enough.

blocks.text: Simple examples, such as testing exam results or checking an average height, help build understanding: data is collected from samples, analysed with basic tests and conclusions are drawn clearly.
Advanced tests: F-test and chi-square test

Advanced tests handle more complex data. The F-test compares the variances of two groups and is used in analysis of variance (ANOVA): F = s1^2 / s2^2, where s1^2 and s2^2 are the two sample variances. For two groups of students with variances 16 and 9, F = 16 / 9 = 1.78, which is compared with a critical value from the F-table to decide whether the variances differ significantly. The chi-square test checks relationships in categorical data.
Numerical example: has a new teaching method improved marks?
The previous average was 70. A sample of 10 students taught with the new method scored 72, 75, 78, 74, 77, 80, 76, 79, 81 and 78.

items: Hypotheses: H0: mu = 70 (no improvement); H1: mu > 70 (improvement).
Standard deviation: the squared deviations from 77 add up to 70, so s = sqrt(70 / 9) = 2.79.
Decision: the p-value for t = 7.93 with 9 degrees of freedom is approximately p = 0.00002, far below 0.05, so H0 is rejected.
Conclusion: the new teaching method significantly improved students' marks.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints p = 0.00002, which is the two-tailed value. The test is one-tailed (H1: mu > 70), so the p-value for t = 7.93 and df = 9 is about 0.000012 (about 0.00001). The decision, reject H0, is unchanged.
